articles.title: Google Sees Ad Revenue Decline Due to AI Mode and Overviews
articles.summary: The decline is attributed to lower monetization rates in AI Mode and Overviews, which prioritize summarized responses over traditional ad-clicking behavior.
articles.content: Google's quarterly earnings call revealed that despite an increase in searches, ad revenue has taken a hit due to users opting for AI Overviews and AI Mode. The reason behind this decline is attributed to lower monetization rates in these newer search features, which prioritize summarized AI responses over traditional ad-clicking behavior further down the page. This phenomenon isn't new; it's been observed that when users type questions into Google, a summarized AI response often appears immediately, reducing the likelihood of clicking on ads placed below the results. To combat this trend, Google is expanding its advertising approach in AI Mode to more countries. The company has announced plans to introduce ads in 10 new countries, including Australia, Canada, India, Kenya, and Singapore. Additionally, Google aims to launch multiturn ads in the US, allowing ads to appear within follow-up queries when a search or conversation has commercial relevance, effectively integrating sponsored content into users' searches. Google's AI Mode is designed to gather more information during conversations about products, allowing for more targeted ads that cater to a user's specific interests. The AI-powered overviews can now display ads on initial queries, not just follow-up questions, and the ads will only appear if there's clear purchase intent. If no commercial relevance is detected, ads won't be shown at all. As Google increasingly relies on its AI tools, users may find it harder to access content from preferred publishers directly through search results. Instead of clicking on links "below the fold," readers may need to dig deeper and explore beyond Google's products. SEO expert Lily Ray warns that Google's AI Mode isn't designed to provide exact links to desired articles. However, users can still navigate around this by scrolling down to traditional search results or using web filters to view a list of links. To mitigate the impact, Ray recommends setting up preferred sources in your Google account settings, which will allow you to see more content from those publications in your personalized results. Google's dominance in search engine market share remains unchallenged, with nearly 90% of global searches passing through its platforms. The company reported a significant increase in year-over-year query volume growth during the third quarter, marking one of the fastest rates in the past five years. However, this trend has had an unexpected consequence: the launch of AI Overviews in May 2024 has led to a decline in advertising revenue for Google. This shift towards relying on artificial intelligence to provide answers directly within search results has resulted in fewer users clicking through to external websites. The impact is most pronounced for online publishers, with many experiencing a substantial decline in website traffic. In fact, the data suggests that AI Overviews now account for nearly half of all Google search queries, leading to a 61% drop in raw traffic volume to other pages. Google's shift towards AI-powered search results has significant implications for how users interact with the platform and the types of content they see. In addition to the traditional search results page, which often features an AI Overview at the top, Google also offers a conversational interface called AI Mode. This mode is accessible through the AI Mode button on the Google home page or by selecting it from the horizontal menu on other Google pages. When users engage with AI Mode, they are presented with a more interactive and in-depth experience than what's available in traditional search results. For instance, if a user asks for information about a specific topic, such as the northern lights, they may receive a map and list of locations with pros and cons, rather than just an overview and links to other websites. This conversational approach is designed to provide more advanced reasoning and ways of interacting with Google's search results. However, this shift also means that users are less likely to click on organic search engine results, which are the non-paid listings that appear at the top of a traditional search results page. As a result, Google will be aggressively routing users toward advertisers rather than publisher links, leading to an even greater decline in organic click-through rates. As a result of this shift in strategy, websites and publishers will find it increasingly difficult to reach their target audience through organic means. Google's algorithm will prioritize ads over publisher links in its AI-powered search results, making it harder for non-paying sites to get noticed. This change is likely to lead to a significant increase in ad visibility, but at the same time, it may drive down user engagement and trust in online content. The impact on publishers and advertisers will be substantial, as they adapt to this new reality where paid promotions take precedence over organic reach. articles.title: NASA's New Space Telescope Set to Launch in 2031
articles.summary: The new telescope from NASA will soon reveal hidden secrets in the night sky by capturing events such as stellar flares and exploding stars.
articles.content: The night sky may appear tranquil to the naked eye, but a new space telescope from NASA will soon change that perception by revealing its hidden secrets in ultraviolet light. The telescope, set to launch in 2031, is designed to capture the fleeting and often catastrophic events that occur in our universe. These events, such as stellar flares and exploding stars, are invisible to us due to their emission of UV radiation, which lies beyond human vision. A backyard telescope may not be able to detect these phenomena, but with the help of specialized technology, astronomers can glimpse them in all their glory. The launch of NASA's new UV space telescope marks a significant milestone in astronomical research, as it will allow scientists to study these previously hidden events in unprecedented detail. By observing the night sky through the lens of UV light, researchers hope to gain valuable insights into the behavior and evolution of stars and galaxies. As we gaze up at the stars, we often fail to notice the cataclysmic events unfolding around us, simply because they emit radiation beyond our visual range. But with NASA's new telescope, these cosmic fireworks will be visible for all to see, shedding light on a universe that is far more dynamic than we ever imagined. The telescope's advanced technology will enable scientists to capture images and data in unprecedented detail, giving them a unique window into the workings of the universe. By studying these events up close, researchers hope to unravel some of the mysteries of the cosmos and gain a deeper understanding of its intricate mechanisms. A new space telescope that specializes in observing ultraviolet light will be launched by NASA in 2031. The UltraViolet EXplorer, or UVEX for short, is a mission led by Caltech that aims to conduct an all-sky survey of near- and far-ultraviolet light. The UVEX mission marks a significant step forward in the exploration of the ultraviolet universe, according to Caltech President Ray Jayawardhana. He described it as "a bold leap" that will help scientists better understand the vast array of light that fills our cosmos. This includes not just visible light but also radio waves and gamma rays. The UVEX telescope is designed to fill a gap in our current understanding of the universe by providing an all-sky survey in ultraviolet light. This will complement surveys conducted by other telescopes, such as the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, which will observe in infrared, and the ESA's Euclid Space Telescope, which will perform three deep-field surveys in visible light. Unlike traditional space telescopes that focus on observing distant objects in exquisite detail, survey telescopes like UVEX play a crucial role in science. They enable scientists to map large areas of the sky, gathering data on millions or even billions of celestial objects. This information is essential for understanding the universe's structure and evolution. The UVEX mission will join several other NASA space telescopes that are currently conducting all-sky surveys. These include SPHEREx, which observes in near-infrared light, and others like the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope and the Vera Rubin Observatory, which will image the night sky repeatedly over a decade. The wealth of data collected by modern astronomy is set to grow even larger thanks to NASA's upcoming UV space telescope, UVEX. Scheduled for launch in 2031, this new addition will significantly enhance our understanding of the universe. According to a white paper outlining the mission, UVEX will conduct a wide-ranging survey of the sky, gathering observations that are up to 100 times deeper than those collected by its predecessor, GALEX. This ultraviolet space telescope's two-year baseline mission is designed to provide a detailed picture of the universe. UVEX's observations will be focused on nearby low-mass galaxies that shine brightly in ultraviolet light. These galaxies play a crucial role in the universe and their study will complement existing research by other telescopes, including the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. This emphasis on low-mass galaxies is one of three core aspects of the UVEX mission. Another key area of focus for the telescope is its ability to rapidly respond to new discoveries in space. The data collected by UVEX will also be used to study individual targets, providing scientists with a more detailed understanding of these celestial objects. The new space telescope being developed by NASA, known as UVEX, is poised to make significant contributions to our understanding of the universe in several key areas. One area of focus will be on low-mass, low-metallicity galaxies, which are characterized by their limited star-forming capabilities and distinct evolutionary patterns. These galaxies play a crucial role in shaping the growth and evolution of the local universe, and scientists hope that UVEX's advanced imaging and spectroscopic surveys will provide valuable insights into how they form and evolve. By studying these galaxies up close, researchers can better understand the complex processes governing their development. In addition to its work on low-mass galaxies, UVEX will also be tasked with exploring the dynamic universe through time-domain surveys. This involves monitoring celestial objects over time to detect transient events such as compact object mergers and stellar explosions. These events are often shrouded in mystery due to their brief duration and faint signals, but UVEX's advanced capabilities will allow it to quickly point at these events and observe them as they unfold. This will provide scientists with a wealth of new data on the environments, energetics, and emission processes involved in these phenomena. The sheer volume of data generated by UVEX is expected to be substantial, rivaling that produced by notable missions like the ESA's Gaia mission. Like Gaia, UVEX's findings are likely to have far-reaching implications for a wide range of research areas, from astrophysics and cosmology to planetary science and more. The launch of UVEX in 2031 marks a significant milestone for astronomers and astrophysicists, as it will be the first new ultraviolet (UV) space telescope in two decades. This state-of-the-art instrument will create detailed deep-sky maps in UV, allowing scientists to study distant objects with unprecedented precision. One of the key features of UVEX is its ability to discern different wavelengths of light coming from distant objects, making it possible to identify specific chemical elements present. This capability will be particularly valuable when studying extreme events such as supernovae and gamma-ray bursts. UVEX's findings are likely to have a significant impact on our understanding of the universe, particularly in areas related to gravitational waves. These ripples in space-time, predicted by Einstein, are generated when extremely dense objects like neutron stars and black holes merge. The UVEX mission will complement existing gravitational-wave observatories by providing UV observations of these events. This will enable scientists to gather more comprehensive data on the properties of these cosmic phenomena. As with any new telescope or mission, there is always a possibility that unexpected discoveries may be made. Scientists are eager to see what insights UVEX will bring to our understanding of the universe, and how its findings will shed new light on some of the most pressing questions in astrophysics and cosmology. The launch of NASA's UV space telescope, known as UVEX, is set to take place in 2031, marking a significant milestone for astrophysics research. Every time scientists observe the universe in a new wavelength, they often discover something unexpected and gain valuable insights into its workings. The UVEX telescope will build upon this principle by providing unprecedented access to ultraviolet radiation from distant galaxies and stars, allowing researchers to study phenomena that are invisible to current telescopes. articles.title: Security breach exposes personal details of over 41,000 DHS employees
articles.summary: A major security breach at the Department of Homeland Security has exposed the personal details of over 41,000 employees, including those working in government cybersecurity.
articles.content: A major security breach at the Department of Homeland Security has exposed the personal details of over 41,000 employees, including those working in government cybersecurity. The breach is believed to be the work of a hacktivist group known as the Department of Peace, who targeted an Okta single sign-on service used by DHS. The hackers stole a vast amount of employee data, including names, contact information and assignments. This sensitive information has been made publicly available through a searchable database called Icepick on the Distributed Denial of Secrets website. The database contains not only personal details but also details about employees' roles, chains of command, and agent identities across various agencies, such as Immigration and Customs Enforcement. The hacktivist group behind the breach, Department of Peace, has described it as an "unprecedented" and "massive exposure of DHS's internal structure. They claim that this dataset will have a significant impact on the department for years to come, making it highly vulnerable to outside scrutiny. The hackers' motivations appear to be linked to their opposition against government-led surveillance, particularly the increasing use of technology by agencies like ICE in their enforcement activities. The Department of Peace has cited DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin's recent statement about ramping up immigration crackdowns as a reason for this breach. The note attached to the leaked files reads: They have our information, so it's only fair that we have theirs." This statement suggests that the hackers are seeking revenge against what they see as unjust surveillance tactics by government agencies. The DHS has confirmed it is investigating a potential security breach that may have compromised sensitive information. In response to the leak, the agency has taken swift action to contain the situation by targeting sites hosting the stolen data, including the searchable archive domain of Icepick. The move aims to prevent further unauthorized access and sharing of the sensitive information. The leaked files are substantial in scope, exposing not only basic contact details but also office addresses, phone numbers, and internal work systems of nearly 41,000 DHS employees. This raises concerns about the potential misuse of this data by malicious actors. The hackers gained access to these sensitive areas through Okta, a secure portal for employee login. As a result, they obtained an inventory of surveillance applications used by ICE, including specialized software such as Penlink and AI tools like ChatGPT and Gemini. The massive DHS breach has sparked a heated debate about institutional legitimacy, with many viewing the exposure as forced transparency against a federal department that has acted with impunity. The release of sensitive information raises questions about accountability and oversight within the government. DHS employees who have been exposed through the Icepick data are not just ordinary personnel, but rather individuals who play key roles in shaping policy and operations within the agency. This strategic release of information highlights the disconnect between those who create policies and those who must implement them on the ground. The public's response to the breach has been telling, with many taking to social media to express support for the hacktivists behind the leak. Comments accompanying an NPR story on the incident reveal a segment of the population that sees the exposure as poetic justice against an agency known for aggressive enforcement and widespread surveillance. As a result of the escalating tensions surrounding government surveillance, tech companies are facing growing pressure to cancel contracts with ICE and DHS agencies. This internal crisis is being driven by employees who are sounding the alarm about the moral implications of working with such entities. The recent breach has also underscored the vulnerability of federal agents and their surveillance toolkits to hacking and leaks. As hacktivists continue to target the infrastructure of these agencies, it remains to be seen how they will respond to this growing threat. A growing number of employees at Boston Dynamics have expressed their discomfort with the company's work being used by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). Hundreds of staff members signed a petition stating they cannot be proud of their work when it is utilized by an agency responsible for mistreating civilians. The recent massive breach of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) cyber systems is not an isolated incident. Earlier this year, the Electronic Frontier Foundation revealed the emergence of groups working on counter-surveillance projects targeting ICE. These initiatives include tools and applications aimed at tracking officers' movements and countering surveillance cameras capable of reading license plates. The Electronic Frontier Foundation emphasizes that individuals are not helpless in the face of government surveillance. Senior Staff Technologist Cooper Quintin noted that even with advanced technologies, there are ways to engage in self-defense against these measures. This message appears to be resonating with hacktivists who continue to target government agencies' infrastructure. As hacktivist efforts escalate, it remains to be seen how the targeted agencies will respond to this growing threat and adapt their strategies to mitigate potential future breaches. articles.title: Breakthrough Achieved in Recycling Silicones
articles.summary: Researchers at TU Berlin have successfully broken down polymer chains of silicone molecules into their basic building blocks using a complex interplay of chemical reaction cycles.
articles.content: A groundbreaking breakthrough has been achieved by researchers at the Institute of Chemistry at TU Berlin who have successfully broken down polymer chains of silicone molecules into their basic building blocks. This innovative process paves the way for recycling silicones, a notoriously difficult task due to their exceptional thermal and chemical stability. The resulting molecule, dimethyldichlorosilane, can be reused as a starting material for producing new silicone compounds. The researchers have applied for a patent for this complex interplay of several chemical reaction cycles that makes the process possible. This achievement has significant implications for green chemistry and the circular economy, with the journal Nature selecting the paper for fast-track online publication. Dr. Martin Oestreich, who led the team, is also a member of the UniSysCat Cluster of Excellence specializing in catalysis at TU Berlin. The market demand for silicone products is substantial, with a total value exceeding 21 billion euros in 2025 and estimated to reach over 33 billion euros by 2033. Silicones possess unique properties that make them ideal for various applications. They exhibit exceptional mechanical properties while reliably repelling water and allowing oxygen to pass through. Silicone products are ubiquitous in everyday life, found in items such as baking pans, baby bottle nipples, gaskets, and medical tubing. The versatility of silicones has driven their widespread use across industries including medicine and industry. The successful testing of the process on various silicone products used in daily life marks a significant milestone for the researchers. With the potential to significantly reduce waste and increase the sustainability of silicone production, this breakthrough is expected to have far-reaching implications. The recycling process for used silicone has long been a challenge due to its robust properties. As a result, waste silicone has typically ended up in landfills or being incinerated. However, this method of disposal not only wastes valuable resources but also poses environmental and health risks. One of the main reasons why complete recycling of silicones is now seen as an important objective is the growing evidence that these materials can be harmful to both the environment and human health when they are disposed of in landfills. On the other hand, producing new silicones requires a significant amount of energy, particularly for extracting elemental silicon from quartz sand at extremely high temperatures. The production process involves extracting elemental silicon from quartz sand at 2,000 degrees Celsius, which is an energy-intensive step. Another crucial component is dimethyldichlorosilane, the basic building block of silicone chemistry. This molecule can be combined to form long chains, with chlorine being replaced by oxygen in a specific reaction. The resulting polymers have a backbone formed not by carbon atoms but by bonds between silicon and oxygen atoms (Si–O–Si–O–Si). The length of these chains can be adjusted, allowing for the creation of different properties. Various molecules can also be attached to the sides of the chains to further customize the characteristics of the resulting silicones. The specific chemistry involved in forming these polymers is distinct from carbon-based chemistry due to the unique bonding between silicon and oxygen atoms. This characteristic allows for a range of possibilities in designing new silicone materials with tailored properties. Breaking down silicone waste into reusable building blocks is a crucial step in creating an ideal recycling process. The researchers have found that to produce new silicones with different properties from end-of-life silicones, the base molecule dimethyldichlorosilane must be the end product of the recycling process. This requires completely breaking down the Si–O–Si chains in the silicones, which is a challenging task due to the stability of silicone materials. A key breakthrough has been achieved through the use of two molecules: a silylium ion as a catalyst and the gas phosgene. The silylium ion facilitates the removal of a chloride ion from phosgene, resulting in the formation of a compound called COCl⁺. This molecule is capable of breaking silicon-oxygen bonds, which are notoriously difficult to break. By doing so, it allows for the release of oxygen as carbon dioxide (CO₂), rendering it unavailable for further reactions and making it easier to manage waste. The immediate release of oxygen as carbon dioxide is a significant advantage of this process, enabling more efficient management of the recycling process and minimizing potential environmental impacts. The reaction to break down silicone waste into reusable building blocks involves a toxic gas called phosgene, but researchers have found a way to manage it by using its solid counterpart, triphosgene. articles.title: Severe Wildfire Season Hits Indonesia Amid El Niño Conditions
articles.summary: Widespread wildfires in Indonesia's Kalimantan region have significant impacts on human health and the environment.
articles.content: Indonesia is grappling with one of its most severe wildfire seasons in over a decade, as El Niño conditions intensify drought across the region. The island of Borneo is among the areas hardest hit by the fires, which are fueled by peatlands smoldering underground in West, Central and South Kalimantan. The widespread wildfires have a profound impact on human health and the environment, releasing smoke haze that poses a significant threat to both. However, the consequences of these fires extend far beyond the initial crisis period. They can fundamentally alter the forests that wildlife relies on for survival, leading to long-term changes in ecosystems. Wild orangutans living in Borneo's forests have been particularly affected by the 2015 wildfires. At the Tuanan Orangutan Research Station, researchers observed firsthand the devastating impact of the fires on their habitats. In the years following the disaster, they documented significant changes in the orangutans' behavior. The research team had a unique advantage when studying the effects of the fires. They had been monitoring a wild orangutan population since 2003, meticulously tracking the animals' movements and recording changes in the forest's health and productivity over time. This extensive dataset allowed them to trace the lasting impact of the wildfires on the orangutans. The researchers have been able to identify significant shifts in the orangutans' behavior following the fires, including reduced travel distances, increased resting periods, and decreased social interaction among individuals. The team at Tuanan research site faced a daunting task in October as they battled to contain the raging wildfires. Emergency workers worked tirelessly to cut firebreaks and pump water onto the fires, but it was a challenging time for orangutan monitoring. Returning to Tuanan after the devastating 2015 fires, Maria van Noordwijk recalled the eerie atmosphere of thick haze that enveloped the region for months. The dense smog blanketed large parts of Southeast Asia, causing widespread disruption and health concerns. The prolonged haze at Tuanan had a profound impact on the orangutans, with many appearing to suffer from respiratory problems. Researchers reported hearing the primates coughing as they struggled to cope with the poor air quality. This was accompanied by changes in their behavior, including reduced travel distances and increased resting periods. As the researchers observed the orangutans over the following years, they began to notice a pattern emerging. The animals were often staying lower in the canopy, possibly seeking refuge from the haze. A crucial discovery made by the team was the significant decline in fruit production that persisted for approximately 2.5 years after the fires. This prolonged shortage may have been caused by a combination of factors, including reduced photosynthesis due to haze and the potential loss of pollinators. The severe wildfires in Borneo have left a lasting impact on the orangutans that inhabit the affected areas. With their primary food source - fruit - scarce due to the prolonged drought and haze, female orangutans were forced to adopt new strategies to conserve energy. They began traveling shorter distances, resting more frequently, and relying on lower-quality fallback foods to survive. Research also revealed a concerning trend: orangutans lost lean body mass as they drew upon their own bodily reserves to meet their energy needs. The fires not only affected the orangutans but also altered the forest landscape. Approximately 15% of Tuanan's forest was destroyed in the 2015 blazes, prompting some orangutans to leave their home ranges and seek refuge elsewhere. This displacement led to increased competition for resources among remaining orangutans, as more individuals converged on a smaller area. Social dynamics began to break down as adult females spent less time foraging together with relatives or younger offspring. The stress of competing for food and space took a toll on social relationships among the orangutans. Adult females became increasingly intolerant and aggressive towards one another in their pursuit of limited resources, leading to potential consequences for reproduction and survival. The recent wildfires in Borneo have led to an alarming loss of older female orangutans, exceeding expectations based on long-term survival rates established during a research study. The devastating impact of these fires is not limited to the immediate dangers posed by flames and smoke; it also extends to the loss of forest habitat, which can lead to reduced food availability and disrupted social relationships among orangutans. This, in turn, forces them to expend energy adapting to their changed environment, a process that can take months or even years. The ongoing 2026 fires have already destroyed an estimated 30% of the study area, a loss that will likely translate into similar pressures faced by orangutans after the 2015 fires. However, it appears that this time around, the toll may be even greater than before. articles.title: Qinghai–Tibet Plateau Terrestrial Animals' Evolution Studied in Detail
articles.summary: A comprehensive study on the evolution of terrestrial animals across the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau has provided a detailed picture of how unique fauna developed over millions of years.
articles.content: A comprehensive study has been conducted on the evolution of terrestrial animals across the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau (QTP), providing a detailed picture of how the unique fauna developed over millions of years. The QTP spans an enormous area of approximately 3.07 million square kilometers, with varying elevations ranging from 88 to 8,848 meters above sea level. This vast region is considered one of the world's most significant biodiversity hotspots and is home to a large number of endemic species that can be found nowhere else. The plateau is divided into three distinct subregions: the plateau platform, the Himalayas, and the Hengduan Mountains. The latter two areas are internationally recognized as biodiversity hotspots due to their exceptionally high levels of endemism. These unique geological formations have created a diverse range of habitats that support an incredible array of plant and animal life, with many species having adapted specifically to these environments over time. The Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (QTP) is a vast and complex region that has long fascinated scientists due to its unique geological history and biodiversity. Previous research on the QTP's evolution has focused primarily on plant species or individual animal groups, leaving a significant knowledge gap in understanding the overall development of terrestrial fauna in the area. To address this gap, researchers created an integrated dataset covering over 20,000 species across five major taxonomic groups: invertebrates, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals. This comprehensive approach allowed them to reconstruct the evolutionary history of 527 endemic terrestrial animal species found exclusively on the QTP. The study revealed that these endemic species have largely developed through a process called in situ diversification, where existing species adapt and evolve within their native environment. The researchers delved deeper into how geological and climatic changes have shaped the evolution of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau's fauna over time. Their findings indicate that the Eocene-Oligocene climate transition, which occurred around 34 million years ago, marked the beginning of sustained diversification and biotic exchange on the plateau. However, this timing varied across the three distinct subregions, reflecting their unique uplift histories and monsoon systems. In regions where rapid uplift occurred, in situ diversification events accelerated significantly. This was observed in the Hengduan Mountains and the Himalayas, where periods of rapid uplift led to a surge in endemic species development. The impact of monsoons on animal migration patterns also varied across subregions. In the Hengduan Mountains, immigration and emigration events peaked during the intensification of the East Asian monsoon, while in the Himalayas they increased and peaked during the intensification of the South Asian monsoon. A comparison with plant evolutionary dynamics revealed a consistent pattern: "plants first, animals later". Early-colonizing plant groups created suitable ecological niches that laid the foundation for animal immigration and diversification. This predictable cross-taxon colonization rule was observed across the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and its subregions. The study of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau's endemic terrestrial fauna has provided a deeper understanding of mountain biota evolution and offers a framework for examining biodiversity in mountain regions globally. This research contributes significantly to our knowledge of how geoclimatic dynamics shape the assembly of unique faunas in high-altitude areas, shedding light on the processes that govern biodiversity worldwide. articles.title: New world discovered beyond Neptune in our solar system
articles.summary: A possible new dwarf planet has been discovered beyond Neptune in our solar system, estimated to be larger than half of Pluto.
articles.content: A possible new world has been discovered beyond Neptune in our solar system, and it could be one of the largest and brightest objects ever found in that region. If confirmed as a dwarf planet, this miniature world would bring the total number of officially recognized solar system dwarf planets to six. The object, designated 2026 ED138, is estimated to have a diameter greater than half that of Pluto, which is currently the largest known dwarf planet. This discovery was made possible by the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's advanced technology, which allowed researchers to see past the millions of stars in the inner Milky Way galaxy. The Rubin Observatory's advanced technology has enabled researchers to scan the entire southern sky every few nights, producing millions of nightly alerts for objects that have changed brightness or position. This capability makes the observatory exceptional in identifying moving objects within our solar system and beyond, including transient events like supernova explosions. In its early stages of operation, the Rubin Observatory had only just begun its 10-year mission to scan the sky when it detected an unusual object, now known as ED138, which stood out in the data collected so far. Holman's software algorithms process the vast amounts of data generated by the observatory, comparing billions of observations to determine if they are detecting the same moving object, a task that requires sophisticated code. By running data from Rubin through this code, researchers identified an unusually large object, which prompted further investigation into its characteristics and behavior. The discovery of thousands of Kuiper Belt objects has provided valuable insights into the early solar system's formation, with these space rocks serving as frozen time capsules holding crucial information about the past. These celestial bodies are significant because they can offer clues to the formation and evolution of our solar system, making them a vital area of study for astronomers. Researchers have been using data from the Rubin Observatory to analyze objects in the Kuiper Belt, which is a region beyond Neptune's orbit where many small, icy bodies reside. The International Astronomical Union has officially recognized five dwarf planets: Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea, and Makemake. However, astronomers studying this area often identify at least nine potential dwarf planets, with several more candidates whose properties remain unknown. While the exact number of dwarf planets is still a topic of debate among astronomers, it's clear that these objects play a crucial role in understanding our solar system's structure and history. Identifying dwarf planets in the Kuiper Belt is challenging due to their remote locations and slow movement from Earth's perspective. The most promising candidates have high surface reflectivity and diameters exceeding 370-500 miles (600-800 km). The object known as ED138 stands out with its estimated size, which ranges between 370-930 miles (600-1,500 km) in diameter. For context, Pluto, the largest recognized dwarf planet, measures approximately 1,477 miles (2,377 km) across. Ceres, the smallest IAU-recognized dwarf planet, has a diameter of around 595 miles (958 km). Further observations will help scientists determine ED138's actual size and density, ultimately deciding if it meets the criteria to be classified as a dwarf planet. articles.title: Día de los Muertos Celebrations Underway in Albuquerque
articles.summary: A garland-making workshop led by Aleja Grajeda is part of the festivities in Old Town as people prepare for Día de los Muertos.
articles.content: As the holiday season approaches, many communities around the world are preparing for Día de los Muertos, a celebration that honors and remembers loved ones who have passed away. The festive atmosphere is palpable in Albuquerque's Old Town, where locals and visitors alike are busy decorating ofrendas with vibrant flowers, candles, and photographs. In a small store nestled in the heart of Old Town, a group of people gathered for a garland-making workshop led by Aleja Grajeda, owner of Las Ofrendas, a business that offers postpartum care, folk medicine, and other services. The room was filled with the sweet scent of copal incense and fresh flowers, creating a serene ambiance that seemed to welcome the spirits. As the participants worked on their garlands, they were surrounded by an assortment of materials, including photos of loved ones, plastic monarch butterflies, and candles. A child's note to a grandmother sat in a frame on one side of the room, adding a touch of warmth and intimacy to the space. The workshop was just one of many activities taking place in Albuquerque as people prepare for Día de los Muertos. This celebration is deeply rooted in Mexican culture and is traditionally observed from October 31 to November 2. During this time, it's believed that the dead can return to their family homes, and the living leave offerings to guide them on their journey. As the workshop participants worked on their garlands, they were given a special task: adding marigolds to complete their creations. These vibrant flowers have been associated with Día de los Muertos for centuries, and their sweet scent is said to help guide deceased ancestors back to their family homes. The store owner brought in a fresh batch of marigolds, which were added to the garlands as the final touch. The bright petals of these flowers add a pop of color to the festive decorations, making them an integral part of the celebration's visual appeal. Marigolds have been used for centuries in various cultures and traditions to ward off evil spirits and guide the dead on their journey. In the context of Día de los Muertos, they play a significant role in helping deceased ancestors find their way back to their loved ones. The significance of marigolds in Día de los Muertos is deeply rooted in their fragrance and appearance. The sweet scent of these flowers is believed to guide the dead on their return journey, while their bright petals add a festive touch to the celebrations. As the workshop came to an end, the participants had completed beautiful garlands adorned with marigolds, candles, and photographs. These delicate creations would soon be placed in homes and public spaces throughout Albuquerque, serving as a reminder of the love and respect that people have for their departed loved ones. The vibrant marigold, often seen in traditional Día de los Muertos celebrations, has its roots in ancient traditions and folklore. In the indigenous language Nahuatl, marigolds are referred to as cempasúchil, which translates to "the flower of 20 petals". This name is a testament to the intricate beauty of these flowers, with their layered petals resembling the complexity of traditional stories and legends. Before Spanish colonization, the Aztecs worshipped a goddess of death named Mictēcacihuātl. Her image was that of a skeleton's face, and she was revered during July and August. Despite the Catholic church's efforts to suppress this worship, it persisted among the Indigenous population. As time passed, people began incorporating their traditional ways of honoring the dead into the Catholic holidays of All Saints' Day and All Souls' Day. This blending of traditions eventually led to the evolution of Día de los Muertos. One of the enduring customs that survived this cultural fusion was the use of marigolds and other flowers to aid the dead on their journey home. These bright orange blooms have been imbued with a range of legends and symbolism. In many cultures, it's believed that marigolds possess the power to guide spirits back to their loved ones. Their strong scent is said to help navigate the soul through the afterlife. The use of flowers in Día de los Muertos celebrations is also deeply rooted in the idea of welcoming the dead into one's home and community. By placing marigolds in public spaces, people are able to honor and respect their departed loved ones. Marigolds have become an integral part of Día de los Muertos festivities, symbolizing love, remembrance, and the connection between the living and the dead. In this way, the humble marigold has transcended its status as a simple flower, becoming a powerful and enduring symbol of cultural heritage. The cultural significance of marigolds in Mexico's Día de los Muertos celebrations is deeply rooted in ancient mythology. One legend tells the story of Tonatiuh, the sun god, who gifted the people with these vibrant flowers to honor their loved ones who have passed away. In another tale, a couple named Xóchitl and Huitzilin are said to have been separated by death, but their love was so strong that it was transformed into a marigold flower. As long as this flower blooms, the couple's love is believed to endure, making marigolds a powerful symbol of eternal devotion. The story goes that Tonatiuh turned Xóchitl into a cempasúchil flower, which remained closed until Huitzilin's spirit returned in the form of a hummingbird. When the flower finally unfurled, its vibrant orange color was revealed to the world, signifying the reunion of the star-crossed lovers. Today, marigolds play a central role in many Día de los Muertos festivities, where they are often used to create elaborate displays and arrangements. In Mexican culture, scents are believed to guide the spirits of the dead back to the land of the living, making marigold petals particularly significant during this time. Marigolds are commonly displayed on ofrendas, in cemeteries, and as garlands, their sweet fragrance filling the air and helping to facilitate the reunion of loved ones. The marigold's layered petals hold significant meaning during Día de los Muertos celebrations. According to traditional interpretations, the multiple layers represent family and the generations that support one another. Each layer of petals also symbolizes love, with the new, delicate petals representing fresh emotions and the older, fading petals signifying past relationships. This dual representation highlights the importance of honoring both the living and the deceased. As part of a Día de los Muertos celebration, marigold garlands are often created to adorn homes and altars. These fragrant flowers are used in various ways, from decorating ofrendas to adorning cemeteries with their vibrant colors. To make these garlands, participants typically start by sipping traditional Mexican chocolate, a beverage that dates back to Mesoamerican civilizations. This rich drink is flavored with chile peppers, a staple ingredient in New Mexican cuisine. The warm and spicy flavors of the chocolate help set the tone for the garland-making process. As participants work on threading marigolds onto strings, they are reminded that their efforts will be appreciated by those who have passed on. During Día de los Muertos, food is left out to welcome ancestors returning from the spirit realm. This gesture acknowledges the long journey these spirits undertake and shows respect for their return. The process of making garlands involves threading marigolds onto strings alongside other flowers like purple blooms and orange slices. These colorful additions create a vibrant display that communicates celebration and hospitality. Baby's breath is another flower often used in Día de los Muertos arrangements, as it pays tribute to children who have passed away. The delicate white petals complement the bright colors of the marigolds and oranges, creating a harmonious visual display. As participants work on their garlands, they are encouraged by the thought that these colorful creations will welcome spirits returning from the afterlife with open arms. Marigolds are an integral part of Día de los Muertos celebrations in Mexico, but their use is not unique to this holiday. Many cultures around the world have a tradition of honoring the dead and celebrating their return from the afterlife. In Celtic cosmology, the time between late October and early November is believed to be a period when the veil between the living and the dead is at its thinnest. This idea is also reflected in European traditions such as Samhain, which was once celebrated with bonfires and the carving of faces into turnips. While these ancient holidays may have been suppressed or replaced by modern celebrations, their legacy lives on in many contemporary customs. Grajeda notes that people around the world have always found ways to honor their dead and connect with loved ones who have passed away. This universal desire to communicate with those beyond the grave is a common thread that runs through many cultures and traditions. Whether it's through elaborate ceremonies or simple gestures, people from all walks of life are drawn to the idea of bridging the gap between life and death. In this context, Día de los Muertos can be seen as just one part of a larger tapestry of human experience. It's a celebration that is open to interpretation and participation, inviting individuals to find their own way to honor their loved ones. While marigolds are an important element in Mexican Día de los Muertos celebrations, they are not the only flowers used during this time. Baby's breath, with its delicate white blooms, is also associated with the holiday and serves as a tribute to children who have passed away. The use of multiple colors and textures in garlands and other decorations adds depth and meaning to Día de los Muertos celebrations. By combining vibrant hues like yellowish-orange, purple, and gold, participants create a visual representation of welcome and celebration that is both beautiful and powerful. Ultimately, the true spirit of Día de los Muertos lies not in its specific traditions or rituals but in the universal desire to connect with those who have come before us. Whether through food, flowers, or other gestures, people from all over the world are drawn to this holiday as a way to honor their loved ones and celebrate the cycle of life. Like the marigolds used during Día de los Muertos, some traditions from Samhain have persisted and evolved over time. Despite efforts to suppress it, the holiday's reverential roots continue to influence modern-day celebrations. articles.title: Chinese Spaceplane Resembles US X-37B Design
articles.summary: A commercial imaging satellite has captured high-resolution images of China's top-secret spaceplane, revealing similarities with the US Space Force's X-37B.
articles.content: A top-secret Chinese spaceplane has been spotted by a commercial imaging satellite, revealing details about its design that closely resemble those of the US Space Force's X-37B spaceplane. The spaceplane, which has delta wings and a payload bay door, bears an uncanny resemblance to its American counterpart. Its dark heat shield and rear-mounted service module with solar arrays further confirm the similarities between the two vehicles. This suggests that China may have studied or even copied aspects of the X-37B's design. The image was captured by Maxar, a company that provides reconnaissance imagery to the US military and intelligence agencies. The satellite's high-resolution view offers a rare glimpse into the Chinese spaceplane's features, which were previously only visible in lower-resolution images. The Pentagon has confirmed that the image is real, releasing it as part of an unclassified report by the Defense Intelligence Agency on threats to the United States in space. However, the report does not reveal any new information about what the spaceplane is used for or its capabilities. China's space program has been ramping up in recent years, with four spaceplane missions launched since 2020. The latest mission, which launched in February, remains in orbit today and has a duration of around nine months. The Chinese spaceplane is shrouded in secrecy, and it's unclear whether there's one or multiple units in service. In contrast, the US Space Force has two X-37B vehicles that have been used on eight missions to date, with the longest-running mission lasting nearly two-and-a-half years from launch to landing. Details about the X-37B's design and capabilities are publicly available, including photos released by US officials and information about its dimensions. However, most of its activities in space remain classified. China's spaceplane operates similarly to the X-37B, launching inside a rocket payload shroud before deploying as a satellite in orbit. A key advantage of spaceplanes like China's is their enhanced maneuverability, making them more suitable for certain missions than traditional satellites, according to a report from the Defense Intelligence Agency. China's spaceplane program has made significant strides in recent months, with the vehicle demonstrating its ability to catch objects in orbit. According to an analysis of open-source orbital tracking data, the Chinese spaceplane released a sub-satellite in June and successfully recaptured it in July. This feat was repeated in August and September, showcasing the spaceplane's capability for orbital maneuvers and object capture. The demonstration highlights the advanced technology behind China's spaceplane program, which has been shrouded in secrecy. The official name of the Chinese spaceplane remains a mystery, with Western publications referring to it as Shenlong based on reports from the 2000s about China's development of a robotic spaceplane. In contrast, Chinese state media refer to the vehicle as Chongfu Shiyong Shiyan Hangtian Qi, or CSSHQ, meaning reusable experimental spacecraft. The Secure World Foundation has published a fact sheet detailing the terminology used by Chinese state media to describe the spaceplane. The foundation's document highlights the complexity of nomenclature surrounding China's space program and the challenges it poses for international observers. The development of advanced space capabilities by China's military is being closely monitored by international observers, who are seeking to understand the implications of these technologies for global security. China's pursuit of anti-satellite technology, also known as "counterspace" weapons, has been identified as a key area of concern. This includes the use of directed-energy weapons (DEWs), which can be used to permanently or temporarily disable a satellite. The potential applications of DEWs in space are varied and concerning. One possible use is to dazzle sensors on an adversary's satellite, rendering it unable to gather critical information. China has reportedly developed ground-based laser systems with varying power levels that can disrupt, degrade, or damage satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO). China has also been testing anti-satellite missiles and has demonstrated the capability to refuel a satellite in geosynchronous orbit, a feat no other country has achieved above LEO. This development marks an important milestone in China's space program and highlights its growing capabilities. In addition to these developments, China has tested a robotic arm that could be used to snag a spacecraft out of orbit, raising concerns about the potential for on-orbit capture and manipulation. The country is also operating a fleet of satellites called TJS that are capable of approaching foreign spacecraft. The United States has been making progress in overcoming limitations related to its inspector satellites in geosynchronous orbit. The US Space Force has recently acquired additional satellites that can be refueled, allowing for greater maneuverability and potentially expanding their capabilities. This development comes as the Pentagon has acknowledged fielding weapons in space, marking a significant milestone for the United States. According to Air Force Secretary Troy Meink, the country is now the first nation to openly possess orbital weapons. This move highlights the growing importance of space-based military assets. Russia is also actively pursuing its own orbital combat program, with ambitions that include deploying nuclear weapons in space. US intelligence officials have confirmed this intention, indicating a heightened level of competition between the two nations in space. articles.title: Amazon's stock price falls after disappointing earnings report
articles.summary: Amazon reported third-quarter revenue of $201.9 billion, slightly below expectations, with profit falling short at $20.7 billion.
articles.content: Amazon's stock price took a hit on Thursday as investors grew concerned about the e-commerce giant's massive spending on artificial intelligence (AI) data centers and weaker advertising performance. The company reported third-quarter revenue of $201.9 billion, slightly below expectations, and its profit fell short at $20.7 billion. This decline was attributed to gains made a year ago from Amazon's investment in AI company Anthropic. Despite this, Amazon Web Services (AWS), the cloud computing unit, continued to thrive, with sales rising 39.3% to $45.98 billion, exceeding Wall Street targets. The strong demand for AWS services, particularly those tied to AI, remains a key driver of growth. However, Amazon's relentless spending on AI infrastructure is starting to raise eyebrows among investors. The company has reaffirmed its expectations that capital expenditures will reach about $220 billion in 2026, with the majority allocated towards AI data centers. The performance of non-cloud businesses, including advertising and holiday-quarter operating profit, is also under scrutiny, having missed analyst expectations. Amazon's heavy spending on AI infrastructure has pushed its free cash flow into negative territory, a stark contrast to last year when it was $14.8 billion positive. Shares of Amazon initially plummeted by 5% in after-hours trading following the release of its latest earnings report. The tech giant's financials come on the heels of similar reports from Microsoft and Alphabet, the parent company of Google, which also showcased robust growth in their cloud units and substantial investments in AI infrastructure. This trend suggests that the demand for artificial intelligence compute remains extremely high, prompting companies to continue pouring significant amounts of money into this area. As one of the largest spenders on data center construction, Amazon has been shifting its focus towards building out AI hubs. The company's capital expenditures are expected to contribute significantly to a projected $700 billion total spent by hyperscalers like Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Meta Platforms in 2026. Amazon's latest financial projections indicate that it anticipates sales ranging from $240 billion to $247 billion for the current quarter, with operating income predicted to fall between $28.5 billion and $33.5 billion. This lower-than-expected operating income range has raised some eyebrows among analysts who had initially forecasted higher numbers. The timing of Amazon's annual Prime Day event this year may also have had a bearing on its third-quarter results, as it was held in the second quarter instead of its usual slot in the third quarter. Amazon's cloud computing unit is facing increased pressure to demonstrate strong growth rates as a result of the AI boom, which has put the spotlight on its ability to keep pace with its peers. The company's reliance on Amazon Web Services (AWS) for AI compute is evident in the prospectus filed by Anthropic, a lab that plans to spend at least $110 billion on AWS services over the next decade. This commitment is part of Anthropic's broader plan to invest at least $389.9 billion in cloud computing with major players like Microsoft and Alphabet. Amazon has invested heavily in AI research through its investments in companies like Anthropic, committing around $18 billion to date, with a potential for an additional $15 billion. However, the company's growth rates have slowed down due to its early mover advantage in cloud computing. As Amazon enters its critical holiday quarter, which accounts for most of its yearly revenue, it is gearing up for e-commerce demand peaks by hiring 300,000 workers. The company has recently introduced a range of hardware products, including Alexa tablets and the Bee AI wearable, as part of its efforts to boost sales. Despite this hiring spree, Amazon is also undertaking significant job cuts in other areas, with around 250 positions eliminated in its devices and services division this week, following earlier layoffs in retail. The company had previously shed about 30,000 workers between late 2025 and early this year. Amazon has begun to shift its focus towards a more strategic approach to artificial intelligence (AI). This change in tack is evident in the company's decision to block Meta's AI assistant, Muse, from accessing its online store in September. By doing so, Amazon aims to protect its core business model, which relies heavily on human interaction and advertising revenue. In a bid to foster a more outcome-driven culture within its software engineering team, Amazon has issued an internal memo emphasizing the importance of embracing AI while prioritizing tangible results. The company is urging its engineers to focus on developing solutions that benefit from current AI tooling rather than simply generating code or consuming tokens. This approach reflects a growing recognition within the industry that AI should be leveraged as a means to drive business outcomes, not merely as an end in itself. By encouraging engineers to think critically about where AI can and cannot add value, Amazon is seeking to cultivate a more informed and adaptable workforce. This shift in mindset should ultimately help the company stay ahead of the curve in an increasingly competitive market, where innovation and strategic decision-making will be key drivers of success. articles.title: US Executive Caught Up in International Espionage Case Involving China's Government
articles.summary: The US government is investigating Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and data center executive who works for Megaspeed, over allegations of funneling information to the Chinese government while facilitating the sale of advanced Nvidia chips.
articles.content: A top executive at Nvidia has been caught up in a high-stakes international espionage case involving China's government. The US government is reportedly investigating Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and data center executive who works for Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that buys chips from Nvidia to power its data centers. Megaspeed's data centers sell computing services to several prominent Chinese AI labs, including Qwen AI maker Alibaba. Unbeknownst to Jensen Huang, the CEO of Nvidia, Alice Huang had developed a close relationship with him, which has raised suspicions about her true intentions. US intelligence agencies have been monitoring Huang's activities electronically. According to reports, officials discovered that Huang was allegedly funneling information to the Chinese government in Beijing while also facilitating the sale of advanced Nvidia chips to China. The transfer of these chips is believed to be a violation of US law, sparking an investigation into Megaspeed and its ties to the Chinese AI industry. Details about what specific information Alice Huang may have shared with China are scarce at this time. However, officials confirm that an ongoing investigation and surveillance of her activities are taking place. The full scope and potential value of the information she provided remain unclear. The US government's lack of warning to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang about the situation has raised eyebrows. Sources suggest that revealing the suspicion could have compromised the US investigation into Megaspeed, making it a delicate matter for officials handling the case. Nvidia's involvement in a suspected espionage case has sparked concerns about the use of AI technology in international trade and conflict. The company's interactions with its customers, including Megaspeed, are being scrutinized, but an Nvidia spokesperson says they are "not unusual or unexpected" given the CEO's frequent communication with thousands of customer executives every year. Nvidia maintains that it treats all its regional cloud customers equally, and that sensitive trade secrets are not shared with them. The company is confident that if the US government believed any individual was a threat to American industry, they would be informed accordingly. The incident highlights the increasing importance of AI technology in global trade, with many experts warning about the potential risks and consequences of its use. This concern is echoed by recent events, including the FBI's arrest of a Saudi Arabian national accused of planting a recording device at an OpenAI executive meeting. As major tech companies continue to invest heavily in AI infrastructure, concerns about the environmental impact and public backlash against data centers are growing. The high demand for advanced computer chips has led to increased costs for RAM and storage, which are being passed on to consumers by hardware manufacturers. The Biden administration's efforts to restrict China's access to advanced computer chips have been met with mixed results. The ban on sales of certain Nvidia chips to China was implemented in 2022, but the rules were relaxed by President Trump in 2025. As a result of these relaxed regulations, the US government now receives 15% of revenue from Nvidia and AMD for chip sales to China. However, reports indicate that some unauthorized activities are still taking place, involving the smuggling of banned chips from the US to China. The investigation into this matter has been ongoing, with The Times reporting that Trump was briefed on the case a year ago but chose not to take any action, despite his close ties to Big Tech leaders like Jensen Huang. articles.title: Ethan Hawke's Laid-Back Holiday Style
articles.summary: Celebrity style is never off-duty, even during the holiday season or awards season, as seen in Ethan Hawke's recent look that draws comparisons to the iconic film Dead Poets Society.
articles.content: Celebrity style is never off-duty, even during the holiday season or awards season. A-listers are constantly on the move, attending screenings, press junkets, and other high-profile events. They can be spotted at upscale venues like SoFi Stadium, where they often take a break from their hectic schedules to kick back in comfort. From morning runs over the Williamsburg Bridge with Harry Styles to turning up for SAG screenings like Ethan Hawke, celebrities are always dressed to impress. Whether it's a high-profile film premiere or a casual outing, stars like Glenn Close and Nicholas Hoult never seem to be out of style. Their fashion sense is on full display as they navigate their busy schedules. The holiday season is the perfect time to take inspiration from these style icons. Maybe you've been eyeing corduroy pants for your wardrobe, or perhaps it's time to dig out those vintage graphic tees that have been collecting dust in your closet. Whatever your sartorial itch, let these celebrities be your guide. Ethan Hawke is a prime example of how to incorporate corduroy into your wardrobe with style. His recent look has drawn comparisons to the iconic film Dead Poets Society, where Robin Williams' character famously wore corduroy as part of his eccentric persona. Hawke's take on the trend is distinctly laid-back. Hawke's outfit consists of a worn-in corduroy suit paired with a faded graphic tee and tinted shades, giving off a relaxed, stoner-chic vibe. His look is a far cry from the more formal, professorial tone that his character might evoke in a different context. Incorporating laid-back style into his wardrobe, this celebrity has opted for well-worn dark brown Sambas instead of traditional dress shoes. These casual kicks perfectly complement his acorn-colored suit, creating a unique and eye-catching look. The combination of earthy tones in the outfit is intentional, as it adds to the relaxed vibe that's perfect for everyday wear. The overall effect is effortless yet stylish, making this celebrity's look one to emulate. Another style inspiration comes from Julia Garner, who showcases how a flowy, monochromatic palette can be both elegant and interesting. A burgundy trench coat adds just the right amount of color to prevent the outfit from feeling dull or uninspired. By layering a long-sleeved tee under a T-shirt, this celebrity has tapped into the laid-back style of '90s-era skaters. Paired with light-wash jeans, all-white sneakers, and Apple earbuds, the overall look is refreshingly analog in today's digital world. Glenn Close demonstrates how to build an outfit around a statement piece, in her case, a jacket from the iconic film The Natural. With navy slacks, loafers, and a crisp white Oxford shirt added to the mix, she creates a polished yet understated ensemble that exudes timeless sophistication. A charcoal-hued Canadian tuxedo is Nicholas Hoult's go-to choice for in-flight attire, paired with black boots and a dad cap to create a stylish yet laid-back ensemble. This denim-on-denim combination proves to be a reliable solution for those long flights where spills and reclined seats are inevitable. The extra layer of warmth provided by the denim makes it an attractive option for travelers seeking comfort during their journey. Alexander Skarsgård, part of Sweden's acting dynasty, showcases a classic graphic tee paired with Chuck Taylors as his in-flight attire of choice. This timeless combination is elevated by the addition of a louche open trench coat, which adds a touch of sophistication to the overall look. The versatile and stylish outfit created by Austin Abrams features black and brown elements that blend together seamlessly, defying conventional fashion wisdom that these colors do not belong together, resulting in a unique and captivating ensemble. articles.title: Autumn Leaf Coloration Begins in Late September
articles.summary: The process of deciduous trees changing colors is influenced by environmental cues such as temperature, daylight hours, and soil moisture levels.
articles.content: As the seasons change and autumn arrives, deciduous trees prepare for the cold winter months by transforming their lush green canopies into vibrant displays of color. The process begins in late September and continues through November, depending on the location, with trees gradually shedding their summer coats to reveal a kaleidoscope of colors including fiery reds, golden yellows, and deep purples. While the stunning visual effect is undeniable, the scientific explanation behind it is more intricate than meets the eye. The transformation of leaves from green to colorful hues involves a complex interplay of factors that determine the final display. The timing and intensity of this process are influenced by various environmental cues such as temperature, daylight hours, and soil moisture levels. These signals trigger a series of biochemical reactions within the tree that ultimately lead to the breakdown of chlorophyll, allowing other pigments to become visible. In regions with distinct seasonal changes, trees adapt their color displays to suit local conditions, resulting in unique regional palettes and peak foliage periods. The fading of green leaves in autumn is not a transformation into vibrant hues, but rather the exposure of previously hidden pigments due to a decrease in chlorophyll production. This process occurs as temperatures drop and daylight hours shorten, allowing other colors to shine through. The underlying shades are revealed much like sun-bleached hair that fades with time. The absence of chlorophyll allows yellow and orange pigments to become visible, but it's not that the leaves themselves turn these colors. Instead, two types of carotenoids, xanthophylls and carotenes, come into view as chlorophyll production slows down. Xanthophylls are responsible for the yellow color, while carotenes bring about the vibrant orange shades. Carotenoids play a crucial role in this process, and they're not limited to autumn foliage. Carotenes, for instance, give carrots their bright orange color. This similarity highlights the commonality of these pigments across different plant species and their environments. The presence of carotenoids is essential for photosynthesis, but they also contribute to the visual palette of leaves. The breakdown of chlorophyll production in trees is a seasonal phenomenon that's not tied to human timekeeping systems like daylight saving time. Despite this, trees seem to have an internal clock that prompts the reduction of chlorophyll levels, allowing other pigments to emerge and take center stage. This process unfolds differently across various regions due to local climate conditions. The interplay between light exposure, temperature, and pigment production gives rise to diverse regional palettes during autumn. In areas with distinct seasonal changes, trees adapt their color displays to suit local conditions, resulting in unique regional peak foliage periods. The breakdown of chlorophyll production in leaves is triggered by an internal clock that prompts trees to shed their green pigment, allowing other colors to emerge. Chlorophyll's disappearance reveals two types of carotenoids: xanthophylls, which produce a yellow color, and carotenes, responsible for the orange hue found in carrots. These pigments have been present in leaves all along but were overshadowed by chlorophyll during the growing season. The vibrant reds and purples that characterize autumn foliage are not always visible, as they only emerge when specific conditions are met. Anthocyanins, a type of pigment produced in response to sugar accumulation in leaves, contribute to these rich colors. As temperatures drop and daylight hours shorten, trees begin to constrict the veins that carry sap in and out of their leaves. At the same time, photosynthesis generates glucose, which accumulates in the leaf and triggers anthocyanin production. The acidity level of a tree's sap affects the final color produced by anthocyanins, resulting in either a scarlet or magenta hue depending on the specific conditions. This process is unique to autumn and contributes to the diverse range of colors seen during this time of year. As temperatures drop and daylight hours shorten, trees prepare for the cold winter months ahead by slowing down their food-making process. This slowdown causes the veins that carry sap into and out of the leaf to constrict, affecting the flow of nutrients. The reduction in nutrient circulation also impacts photosynthesis, which typically occurs during sunny fall days when trees are actively producing glucose. With less glucose being produced, sugars accumulate within the leaf cells, creating conditions ripe for the production of anthocyanins. Anthocyanins are responsible for the red and purple hues seen in some deciduous trees during autumn. However, not all tree species can produce these deeper shades, with some only reaching yellow or gold due to their genetic makeup. Deciduous trees like sugar maples, dogwoods, and sweetgums have a higher likelihood of displaying reddish-purple foliage thanks to their genetic predisposition. This is in contrast to most other deciduous trees that tend to turn yellow or gold as the seasons change. As leaves near the end of their life cycle, they exhaust their stores of chlorophyll, carotenoids, and anthocyanins. The remaining compounds contribute to a dull brown coloration visible to the naked eye, driven by waste products known as tannins that are also found in red wine. As autumn progresses, trees undergo a critical process to prepare for winter's chill. They form a thin layer of cells at the base of each stem, effectively sealing themselves off from the rest of the tree. This process, known as abscission, is a vital mechanism that allows the tree to conserve energy and nutrients during the harsh winter months. The formation of this cell layer marks the beginning of the end for the leaves, which are gradually cut off from the tree's nutrient supply. As the leaves wither and die, they fall to the forest floor, where they decompose and contribute to the soil's fertility. articles.title: Breakthrough in Plant Biology Could Provide Safer Alternative to Forever Chemicals
articles.summary: Scientists have been searching for greener alternatives to PTFE due to concerns over its long-term persistence and impact on human health.
articles.content: A breakthrough in plant biology could soon provide a safer alternative to forever chemicals like PTFE used in waterproof clothing. Scientists have been searching for greener alternatives due to concerns over the long-term persistence of these substances in the environment and their impact on human health. The properties that make PFAS so useful, such as high heat resistance and water- and greaseproof qualities, are being matched by researchers who are looking to nature for inspiration. The search has led them to suberin, a plant-based substance that transports water across long distances within plants. Suberin's super-waterproof surface is formed from a combination of fatty acids and lignin, the plant polymer. Joshua Yuan, a chemical engineer at Washington University in St Louis, Missouri, explains how suberin works: "Plants transport water across very long distances using this structure called suberin." This unique substance has sparked interest among researchers who are working to replicate its properties in man-made materials. They believe that such a development could provide a safer and more sustainable alternative to PFAS. The potential applications of suberin-inspired waterproof coatings are vast, from clothing and cookware to medical tools and electrical insulation. While the research is still in its early stages, scientists are optimistic about the possibilities of harnessing nature's ingenuity to create greener technologies that minimize harm to human health and the environment. Researchers have been exploring ways to replace per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) with more environmentally friendly alternatives. One promising approach involves mimicking nature's waterproof coatings found in plants such as roots and stems. Scientists have discovered that the plant-based coating, known as suberin, is made up of a combination of paper industry waste and animal fat. This unique blend creates a water-repellent barrier when applied to surfaces. When tested on glass, metal, and cotton, the coating demonstrated excellent waterproofing properties. The mechanism behind this natural coating's effectiveness differs significantly from PFAS-based materials. Instead of relying on carbon-fluorine bonds to repel water molecules, the suberin-like slurry creates a precisely nanostructured surface with numerous tiny air pockets. This structure minimizes direct contact between the coated material and water droplets, much like the lotus effect seen on plant leaves. The results showed that the new coating was resistant to contamination by limescale and mechanical wear, while also offering similar water resistance to state-of-the-art PFAS coatings such as PTFE. As textiles are one of the first industries expected to be impacted by PFAS restrictions, this alternative could prove particularly useful in the near future. The bio-based coating made from suberin is being considered for various applications, including food packaging such as internal linings of drinks cans. However, its lower heat tolerance compared to PTFE means it's not suitable for bakeware at this time. The team is exploring the potential uses of this material further, and its completely bio-based nature is a significant advantage according to one researcher. The coating can be easily degraded under composting conditions, breaking down without releasing any harmful residues into the environment.
